canonical_name: Weyl character formula family for finite-dimensional highest-weight representations
literal_source_claim_zh: 李群表示的特征标公式
literal_source_claim_en: A character formula for Lie-group representations.
statement_blocker: The catalog does not select a compact Lie-group or complex semisimple Lie-algebra formulation; fix the group, Lie algebra, representation and highest-weight hypotheses; choose a maximal torus or Cartan subalgebra and positive roots; define the weight lattice, Weyl group, sign, and Weyl vector; or choose a formal-character versus pointwise quotient identity and its denominator domain. The inspected modern formal-character theorem is a strong source lead but is not cited by the catalog and has no approved checked Lean transport. Selecting an exact proposition at intake would invent or substitute mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: an approved source must select a compact connected Lie group, complex semisimple Lie algebra, or algebraic group; coefficient field and universe; finite-dimensional irreducible representation or highest-weight module; maximal torus or Cartan subalgebra; and the associated root and weight data.
conclusion: Open: an exact formal-character identity or a pointwise character evaluation equating the irreducible highest-weight character with the source-defined alternating Weyl numerator and denominator; representation, equality domain, and formula encoding are unresolved.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before a proposition is selected; the statement phase must resolve every case listed in scope-map.md.
candidate_scope_not_credited: the formal character of the irreducible finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie-algebra module of dominant integral highest weight lambda equals the alternating Weyl numerator divided by the Weyl denominator
the restriction to a maximal torus of an irreducible finite-dimensional representation of a compact connected Lie group is given on regular torus elements by the pointwise Weyl quotient
a denominator-free cross-multiplied identity in an integral group algebra
the generalization to reductive groups or algebraic groups
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: rank-zero or trivial group and Lie algebra
zero highest weight and the trivial representation
singular torus elements where the pointwise denominator vanishes
representations that do not integrate or descend through a central quotient
formal equality versus analytic equality and maximal-torus versus full-group equality
excluded_substitutions: Weyl dimension formula or the Weyl denominator identity alone
Peter-Weyl completeness or the highest-weight classification
Weyl-Kac, Kac-Peterson, Kazhdan-Lusztig, Macdonald, or affine character and denominator formulas
finite-group character orthogonality or trace identities
root-system, weight-space, or Weyl-group infrastructure alone
LieAlgebra.LieCharacter, which is a Lie homomorphism to scalars and not a representation character
rank-one, fixed-type, trivial-representation, or numerical special cases
a structure or hypothesis storing the desired formula
the catalog's untrusted verified label or the discovery probe as proof credit
